question: Is the excess third-and-later-stop spatial deepening of route-new species carried mainly by taxa that reach overlapping/full chorus intensity (CallingIndex 2-3) in the wet survey?

samples.robust: Intersection of same-observer pairs and pairs with all ten identical nonmissing SiteID values.

species_definition: For each route-new species absent from the entire dry route, let k be its number of occupied wet stops and m be its maximum wet CallingIndex across those stops.
model: Each pair-level component uses the existing matched-pair model with rain_contrast, temperature_difference, day_of_year_difference, year_gap, State and RunNumber; route-clustered covariance.
primary_rule: Strong-chorus spatial deepening is supported if third_plus_strong has a positive rain_contrast coefficient with complete 95% CI >0 and contributes >50% of the total third_plus rain coefficient.
robustness_rule: The same primary rule must hold in the same-observer + physical-stop subset for joint robustness.
secondary: Report CI3-present component separately; no additional pass gate.
interpretation: Support links the spatial-depth excess to substantial chorus activation rather than to CI1-only marginal detections.
This is an observed-component decomposition, not a new null-model family.
CallingIndex is ordinal acoustic intensity, not exact abundance or reproductive success.
No causal rainfall or physiological mediator is identified.
